tickets.title: Delivery worker e-bikes obstructing 11th Street
tickets.requester: Susan Cestor (District Manager); Keith Powers (Assembly Member); Board member (unnamed)
tickets.summary: Over a hundred e-bikes used by food delivery workers are stored on 11th Street, blocking the street and sidewalk and spreading to nearby corners, with businesses closing and landlords unable to rent units. Enforcement and sanitation are planned for October 7, while speakers asked for advance warning in languages the workers read and for a legal parking or corral site. The district manager has worked on this since February 2024 and has found no site yet. Action: The board should follow up with the precinct, DOT, and sanitation on notice, translated outreach, and a legal storage site for the delivery workers' bikes.

tickets.title: Drug activity and lighting in Seward Park
tickets.requester: Susan Cestor (District Manager); Board member (unnamed); Parks committee member (unnamed)
tickets.summary: Residents and park users report increased drug use and more homeless people in Seward Park, including near the restroom beside the Ecology Center, and a speaker noted dark spots with few lights. The district manager said police are stationed there under a task force and that outreach and harm reduction providers are active. A board member asked whether mobile crisis teams could respond instead of police. Action: The board should ask the precinct, Parks, and DOT to address the drug activity and park lighting and to report whether mobile crisis teams can be used.

tickets.title: Allen Street full liquor license denial recommendation
tickets.requester: Michelle Cooper Smith (board member); Board member (unnamed)
tickets.summary: The board voted 20 to 10 with 9 abstentions to recommend outright denial of a full liquor license for the 11 Allen Street operator, citing a saturated area, problems at the operator's prior location near Canal Street, and a nearby temple that does not count for the 200 foot rule. Committee members noted that without a board denial the SLA could approve the license without the stipulations, and that a denial needs community members to appear at the SLA. Action: The community board office will organize residents to attend the SLA hearing in support of the denial and will pull 311 complaint records for the file.

tickets.title: August SLA resolution wording corrections for two items
tickets.summary: The SLA committee chair reported two clerical errors in August resolutions: item 10 for Soft Hours Tea House and item 3 for Cozy Cafe, both of which should refer to beer and wine licenses rather than full on-premises licenses. The error was caught by a board member before the meeting. Action: None; the corrected wording was announced at the meeting.

tickets.title: Manhattan Bridge exits and Canal Street redesign update
tickets.summary: The transportation committee sent a letter to the mayor and DOT restating community concerns at the foot of the Manhattan Bridge after a recent crash and death, and asking for an update on the Canal Street redesign. The committee has not received an update on the redesign since January. Action: The board should press DOT for a response to the Manhattan Bridge concerns and an update on the Canal Street redesign.

tickets.title: Essex Market RFP issuance postponement
tickets.summary: A joint land use and economic development meeting found EDC unprepared to explain how the board's two resolutions were reflected in the Essex Market RFP, which was due to go out at the end of the month. The committee asked EDC to postpone issuance so the RFP can require a community market. Action: The board should meet with EDC later this week to confirm the RFP includes the resolution terms and report back.

tickets.title: Pilot public restrooms in district
tickets.location_raw: Delansancy Plaza; Cooper Square at East, Sixth, Street, Third, Avenue
tickets.requester: Mayor's Office representative (unnamed); Transportation and equity committee chair (unnamed)
tickets.summary: DOT is installing two free pilot public restrooms in the district, one near Delansancy Plaza and one at Cooper Square, with a private contractor keeping them clean for a year. The committee raised concerns about access rules and emergency calls, and the mayor's office asked for suggestions on good nonprofit locations for the tap cards. Action: The board should vote on a resolution next month setting out how the restroom pilot should be handled.

tickets.title: Congestion pricing impact on FDR Drive
tickets.summary: A board member asked whether congestion pricing increased congestion on the FDR, the one location the earlier air quality report projected would see more traffic, and whether any reporting is planned. A prior board resolution addressed the FDR impacts. Action: The board should ask MTA and DOT whether projected FDR congestion occurred and request any planned reporting.

tickets.title: Third Avenue L train stop closure pilot
tickets.summary: A public speaker who built a simulation from MTA trip data argued that closing the L train stop at Third Avenue would save New Yorkers about 1,800 hours a day because few riders board or alight there. He asked the board to raise it with the transportation committee and to request a pilot closure with the MTA. Action: The board should refer the Third Avenue stop closure proposal to the transportation committee and ask the MTA about a pilot.

tickets.title: Indoor roller skating venue on East River Pier
tickets.location_raw: East River Pier across from the Katherine Slip Mall
tickets.summary: A public speaker proposed a 300,000 square foot, three-story indoor roller skating and multi-use building on the East River Pier, with $8 admission and projected 250 to 500 jobs. The proposal responds to the loss of indoor skating rinks to real estate costs. Action: The board should refer the pier proposal to the land use committee for review.

tickets.title: Food and communication access for NYCHA residents
tickets.summary: A public speaker in NYCHA housing described struggling with lack of food, water, and necessities and difficulty finding work. A hard-of-hearing speaker said communication access, including interpretation for deaf residents, is essential for the community. Action: The board should ask the relevant agencies what food and necessities support is available for NYCHA residents and how communication access can be provided.

tickets.title: Mobile voting option for CEC elections
tickets.requester: Health and Human Services committee chair (unnamed); Board member (unnamed)
tickets.summary: A resolution before the board supports a mobile-first voting option for Community Education Council elections because turnout has been around 2 percent and many households rely only on smartphones. Speakers also raised equity, outreach in multiple languages, and reassurance that immigration status is not collected. Action: The board should vote on the resolution and send it to the NYC Department of Education urging a mobile voting pilot and expanded parent outreach.

tickets.title: Annual district needs and budget priorities vote
tickets.summary: The district manager said the board will vote in October on its district needs statement and ranked expense and capital budget priorities for each city agency, after meeting with over 20 agencies. The draft city housing plan has about 7,000 units over five years, 75 percent of them market rate, while the board's top need is affordable housing. Action: The board should vote on the district needs statement and ranked budget priorities in October and push committees to take proactive positions on housing plans.

tickets.title: Proposed bylaws changes on attendance removal process
tickets.summary: Proposed bylaws changes would handle attendance problems through a letter and an executive committee meeting after the first issue, and remove attendance from the general removal process. The change would also require public members to follow conflict of interest policies. Action: The board will vote on the bylaws changes at the October full board meeting, with notice sent at least 28 days in advance.

tickets.title: Second vice chair election result
tickets.summary: Daniel Tano and Zachary Thomas gave speeches and the board voted by ballot for second vice chair, with Daniel Tano receiving 25 votes and Zachary Thomas 14. The chair congratulated Daniel Tano on the win. Action: None; the election was completed at this meeting.

tickets.title: Board member training requests on SLA and procedures
tickets.summary: The board chair announced planned trainings on SLA, Robert's Rules, and office procedures, with dates to be reported later. Members were asked to email the chair with other training topics. Action: The board chair will report training dates and take member requests for additional training topics.

tickets.title: Mentor assignment for new board member
tickets.summary: The chair welcomed newly appointed board member Leila Mahia and said a mentor will be assigned in the near future. Action: The board office will assign a mentor to Leila Mahia.
